scope: Reserved INFO and FORMAT field inventories for VCFv4.1 through VCFv4.5. VCFv4.1/4.2 are preserved as prose enumerations without fabricated Number/Type attributes; VCFv4.3/4.4/4.5 use explicit Number/Type tables. This artifact does not cover all normative prose or non-reserved custom fields.
method: Imported exact row text, source line, field ID and declared Number/Type (where actually present) from pinned source-derived artifacts. Mechanical transitions compare row IDs, Number, Type and normalized descriptions. Attributes first appearing in a later table are classified as newly_specified rather than semantic changes. Source locators remain version-specific. No backward inference is applied.

rows.description: genotype, encoded as allele values separated by either of $/$ or $\mid$. The allele values are 0 for the reference allele (what is in the REF field), 1 for the first allele listed in ALT, 2 for the second allele list in ALT and so on. For diploid calls examples could be $0/1$, $1\mid0$, or $1/2$, etc. For haploid calls, e.g.\ on Y, male non-pseudoautosomal X, or mitochondrion, only one allele value should be given; a triploid call might look like $0/0/1$. If a call cannot be made for a sample at a given locus, `.' should be specified for each missing allele in the GT field (for example `$./.$' for a diploid genotype and `.' for haploid genotype). The meanings of the separators are as follows (see the PS field below for more details on incorporating phasing information into the genotypes):
rows.raw_source_line: \item GT : genotype, encoded as allele values separated by either of $/$ or $\mid$. The allele values are 0 for the reference allele (what is in the REF field), 1 for the first allele listed in ALT, 2 for the second allele list in ALT and so on. For diploid calls examples could be $0/1$, $1\mid0$, or $1/2$, etc. For haploid calls, e.g.\ on Y, male non-pseudoautosomal X, or mitochondrion, only one allele value should be given; a triploid call might look like $0/0/1$. If a call cannot be made for a sample at a given locus, `.' should be specified for each missing allele in the GT field (for example `$./.$' for a diploid genotype and `.' for haploid genotype). rows.description: genotype likelihoods comprised of comma separated floating point $log_{10}$-scaled likelihoods for all possible genotypes given the set of alleles defined in the REF and ALT fields. In presence of the GT field the same ploidy is expected and the canonical order is used; without GT field, diploidy is assumed. If A is the allele in REF and B,C,... are the alleles as ordered in ALT, the ordering of genotypes for the likelihoods is given by: F(j/k) = (k*(k+1)/2)+j. In other words, for biallelic sites the ordering is: AA,AB,BB; for triallelic sites the ordering is: AA,AB,BB,AC,BC,CC, etc. For example: GT:GL 0/1:-323.03,-99.29,-802.53 (Floats)
rows.raw_source_line: \item GL : genotype likelihoods comprised of comma separated floating point $log_{10}$-scaled likelihoods for all possible genotypes given the set of alleles defined in the REF and ALT fields. In presence of the GT field the same ploidy is expected and the canonical order is used; without GT field, diploidy is assumed. If A is the allele in REF and B,C,... are the alleles as ordered in ALT, the ordering of genotypes for the likelihoods is given by: F(j/k) = (k*(k+1)/2)+j.  In other words, for biallelic sites the ordering is: AA,AB,BB; for triallelic sites the ordering is: AA,AB,BB,AC,BC,CC, etc.  For example: GT:GL 0/1:-323.03,-99.29,-802.53 (Floats)

rows.description: phase set. A phase set is defined as a set of phased genotypes to which this genotype belongs. Phased genotypes for an individual that are on the same chromosome and have the same PS value are in the same phased set. A phase set specifies multi-marker haplotypes for the phased genotypes in the set. All phased genotypes that do not contain a PS subfield are assumed to belong to the same phased set. If the genotype in the GT field is unphased, the corresponding PS field is ignored. The recommended convention is to use the position of the first variant in the set as the PS identifier (although this is not required). (Non-negative 32-bit Integer)
rows.raw_source_line: \item PS : phase set.  A phase set is defined as a set of phased genotypes to which this genotype belongs.  Phased genotypes for an individual that are on the same chromosome and have the same PS value are in the same phased set.  A phase set specifies multi-marker haplotypes for the phased genotypes in the set.  All phased genotypes that do not contain a PS subfield are assumed to belong to the same phased set.  If the genotype in the GT field is unphased, the corresponding PS field is ignored.  The recommended convention is to use the position of the first variant in the set as the PS identifier (although this is not required). (Non-negative 32-bit Integer)

rows.description: phasing quality, the phred-scaled probability that alleles are ordered incorrectly in a heterozygote (against all other members in the phase set). We note that we have not yet included the specific measure for precisely defining ``phasing quality''; our intention for now is simply to reserve the PQ tag for future use as a measure of phasing quality. (Integer)
rows.raw_source_line: \item PQ : phasing quality, the phred-scaled probability that alleles are ordered incorrectly in a heterozygote (against all other members in the phase set).  We note that we have not yet included the specific measure for precisely defining ``phasing quality''; our intention for now is simply to reserve the PQ tag for future use as a measure of phasing quality. (Integer)

genotype, encoded as allele values separated by either of $/$ or $\mid$. The allele values are 0 for the reference allele (what is in the REF field), 1 for the first allele listed in ALT, 2 for the second allele list in ALT and so on. For diploid calls examples could be $0/1$, $1\mid0$, or $1/2$, etc. For haploid calls, e.g.\ on Y, male non-pseudoautosomal X, or mitochondrion, only one allele value should be given; a triploid call might look like $0/0/1$. If a call cannot be made for a sample at a given locus, `.' should be specified for each missing allele in the GT field (for example `$./.$' for a diploid genotype and `.' for haploid genotype). The meanings of the separators are as follows (see the PS field below for more details on incorporating phasing information into the genotypes):
read depth at this position for this sample (Integer)

sample genotype filter indicating if this genotype was ``called'' (similar in concept to the FILTER field). Again, use PASS to indicate that all filters have been passed, a semicolon-separated list of codes for filters that fail, or `.' to indicate that filters have not been applied. These values should be described in the meta-information in the same way as FILTERs (String, no whitespace or semicolons permitted)
changes.to: Filter indicating if this genotype was ``called''

changes.from: genotype likelihoods comprised of comma separated floating point $log_{10}$-scaled likelihoods for all possible genotypes given the set of alleles defined in the REF and ALT fields. In presence of the GT field the same ploidy is expected and the canonical order is used; without GT field, diploidy is assumed. If A is the allele in REF and B,C,... are the alleles as ordered in ALT, the ordering of genotypes for the likelihoods is given by: F(j/k) = (k*(k+1)/2)+j. In other words, for biallelic sites the ordering is: AA,AB,BB; for triallelic sites the ordering is: AA,AB,BB,AC,BC,CC, etc. For example: GT:GL 0/1:-323.03,-99.29,-802.53 (Floats)
the phred-scaled genotype likelihoods rounded to the closest integer (and otherwise defined precisely as the GL field) (Integers)
changes.to: Phred-scaled genotype likelihoods rounded to the closest integer

changes.from: the phred-scaled genotype posterior probabilities (and otherwise defined precisely as the GL field); intended to store imputed genotype probabilities (Floats)
conditional genotype quality, encoded as a phred quality $-10log_{10}$ p(genotype call is wrong, conditioned on the site's being variant) (Integer)
haplotype qualities, two comma separated phred qualities (Integers)

phase set. A phase set is defined as a set of phased genotypes to which this genotype belongs. Phased genotypes for an individual that are on the same chromosome and have the same PS value are in the same phased set. A phase set specifies multi-marker haplotypes for the phased genotypes in the set. All phased genotypes that do not contain a PS subfield are assumed to belong to the same phased set. If the genotype in the GT field is unphased, the corresponding PS field is ignored. The recommended convention is to use the position of the first variant in the set as the PS identifier (although this is not required). (Non-negative 32-bit Integer)

phasing quality, the phred-scaled probability that alleles are ordered incorrectly in a heterozygote (against all other members in the phase set). We note that we have not yet included the specific measure for precisely defining ``phasing quality''; our intention for now is simply to reserve the PQ tag for future use as a measure of phasing quality. (Integer)
comma separated list of expected alternate allele counts for each alternate allele in the same order as listed in the ALT field (typically used in association analyses) (Integers)
RMS mapping quality, similar to the version in the INFO field. (Integer)

semantic_review_findings.finding: The reserved INFO and FORMAT row IDs and descriptions are identical in this mechanical inventory. This does not mean the full versions are semantically identical; the ALT '*' allele change is separately recorded in the genotype/SV crosswalk.

VCFv4.3 formalizes reserved definitions as Number/Type tables. INFO rows AD/ADF/ADR appear; FORMAT rows AD/ADF/ADR/PP appear; GLE is no longer in the reserved FORMAT inventory. The table descriptions are shortened relative to prose enumerations, so detailed semantics must be reconciled against surrounding definitions rather than treated as deleted. Determine the normative status and any deprecation/compatibility meaning of GLE's removal.

The INFO reserved rows are unchanged in the mechanical inventory; FORMAT adds PSL, PSO and PSQ with Number=P. Their semantics must be read jointly with VCFv4.4 allele-level phasing and derivative-chromosome reconstruction prose.

INFO row IDs are unchanged, but END's table description changes to explicitly deprecated/backward-compatibility status. FORMAT adds 44 row IDs, including LEN, local-allele selectors/equivalents, base-modification families and aliases. The 4.5 reserved FORMAT table's xanthosine aliases contain a case inconsistency with prose; see VCF45-FORMAT-XAON-ALIAS-CASE-001.
